column1: As a borrower, I register and log in with email/password or Google
column29:
h2. User story

As a *borrower*, I want to register and log in with email and password or with Google, so that my application and personal details are kept in my own account.

*Brief line:* Mobile: Register/Login: secure client sign-in via email/password or social authentication using Firebase Auth.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Given the sign-up form, when a borrower enters valid details (name, email, password, phone, address, county, Eircode), then a Firebase Auth account is created and a borrower profile with role "borrower" is saved in Firestore.
# A password under 8 characters, or without both a letter and a number, can't be submitted, and the rule is shown under the field.
# Signing in with a wrong password shows "Email or password is incorrect" without saying which is wrong, and "Forgot password?" sends Firebase's reset email (visible in the Emulator UI).
# "Continue with Google" signs a borrower in; a first-time Google user completes the same profile fields (without a password) before reaching the home screen.
# A signed-in borrower stays signed in after closing and reopening the app, and signing out returns to the welcome screen.

h2. Decisions

* *Sign-up fields:* name, email, password, phone, address, county, Eircode. The broker and underwriter need a contactable borrower with an Irish address.
* *Passwords:* at least 8 characters, with a letter and a number. Clear enough to explain on screen, and stronger than Firebase's 6-character minimum.
* *Google sign-in:* yes; the brief asks for social sign-in. Google users complete the same profile.
* *Forgot password:* yes, using Firebase's reset email.
* *Broker:* the borrower picks one after sign-up and can change it later. _Moved to its own story (choose and change my broker) in the backlog review._
* *Later, not this sprint:* accepting terms and conditions, and GDPR consent.

h2. Test case

Against the Firebase Emulator Suite with the seeded users.

# Sign up with Alice Murphy, a new email, a valid password, 087 123 4567, 12 Oak Park, Cork, {{a65f4e2}}. *Expect:* the account is created, and the profile in the Emulator UI has role {{borrower}}, Eircode {{A65 F4E2}} and phone {{+353871234567}}.
# On the password field, type {{abcdefgh}}. *Expect:* "Contains a number" stays unticked and Continue stays disabled. Add a {{1}}. *Expect:* all three rules tick and Continue is enabled.
# Sign in as {{alice@test.com}} with a wrong password, then with an unknown email. *Expect:* both show "Email or password is incorrect".
# Tap Forgot password? for {{alice@test.com}}. *Expect:* "Check your email", and the reset email appears in the Emulator UI under Auth.
# Continue with Google as a first-time user. *Expect:* the same profile fields without a password, then the home screen.
# Close and reopen the app. *Expect:* still signed in. Sign out. *Expect:* the Welcome screen.

column1: As a broker or underwriter, I log in to the web portal and see only the views for my role
column29:
h2. User story

As a *broker or underwriter*, I want to log in to the web portal and see only the pages my role allows, so that I can do my job without seeing tools or files I shouldn't.

*Brief line:* Web: Role-Based Access: independent mortgage brokers and bank underwriting officers get distinct authenticated views.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# The seeded broker and underwriter each sign in with email and password and land on their own dashboard.
# The role comes from the Firebase ID token's {{role}} claim; a borrower account signing in to the portal is refused with "This portal is for brokers and bank staff".
# Opening an underwriter-only URL (stress test, sign-off) as a broker shows a "not allowed" page instead of the content; a Vitest test covers the route guard.
# Signing out returns to the login page, and refreshing the page keeps a signed-in user signed in.

h2. V2 implementation refinement

This supplements the existing user story and acceptance criteria with the inspected V2 design, suggested frontend files and integration boundaries. It does not change the ticket's assignee, sprint, priority or lifecycle status.

*Design:* [Login / Role Selection|https://www.figma.com/design/F6lldwqy172ox5SeALdDEU?node-id=469-1289].

*Shared implementation rules:* Work inside al-web using React, React Router, Tailwind and Firebase. Reuse shared layout/components and the approved tokens in docs/infrastructure.md; preserve V2's hierarchy. Handle loading, empty, pending, permission-denied and failed states without presenting prototype sample data as live results. Suggested .jsx/.js paths may be .tsx/.ts if the actual scaffold uses TypeScript; extend suitable existing files rather than create duplicates.

h3. Suggested files and responsibilities

* pages/LoginPage.jsx; layouts/AuthLayout.jsx — Brand/form layout, accessible email/password form and submission states.
* context/AuthContext.jsx; components/auth/RequireRole.jsx; routes.jsx — Wait for Firebase session and token claims before routing; choose the role-specific landing route and protect deep links.
* services/firebase.js; services/authService.js; services/apiClient.js — Firebase setup, sign-in/out and ID token handling.

h3. Backend connections and dependencies

* [AL-55|https://alprojectcs3.atlassian.net/browse/AL-55] — Dumi: Firebase ID token verification and API 401/403 enforcement.
* [AL-53|https://alprojectcs3.atlassian.net/browse/AL-53] — Existing emulator users/role claims; development Auth on 9099 and Firestore on 8080, project demo-al.
* [AL-85|https://alprojectcs3.atlassian.net/browse/AL-85] — Dumi: profile/application API, exact route contracts and CORS; direct Firestore versus API boundary is still to be agreed.

Agree any unnamed field, collection/subcollection path, endpoint, request/response unit, error shape and live-update boundary with the relevant backend owner before wiring it. Use Firebase token authentication and backend/rules authorisation, not only UI hiding. The checked-in emulator setup is a starting point, not proof that all feature contracts already exist.

h3. Additional acceptance criteria for V2 and integration

# Use the approved shared tokens. Broker landing and underwriter landing are separate protected routes; pending auth shows a loading state and reveals neither role's content.
# Use the trusted role custom claim, never the selected Figma demo role or users document convenience role as authority. Unknown/missing roles and borrower accounts receive a clear refused-access state; refresh, expiry and sign-out do not expose cached protected data.
# Login failures are visible beside the form; prevent duplicate submits and clear role-specific subscriptions/state on sign-out.
# The backend/rules remain the authority even when a route guard exists.

h3. Moved to Sprint 2 (agreed by the team in #meetings and Slack, 19 Oct 2026)

* The V2 split login layout (brand panel beside the form). It was agreed on 13 Oct as a later change.
* Continue with Google and the demo role-entry buttons, which need the separate scope and provisioning decision tracked in AL-192. A visual prototype button does not grant access.
* Sending the Firebase ID token on protected API requests and telling an expired or invalid token (401) apart from permission denied (403). The portal makes no API calls yet, so this waits for its first one; the demonstration of API role denial moves with it.

h3. Evidence and delivery boundary

Vitest covers signed-out, loading, broker, underwriter, borrower and missing-role guards plus deep-link refresh and sign-out. A real seeded broker/underwriter login was verified against the Auth emulator.

Record the matching story test case and actual verification evidence in Nikoloz's own sprint folder/summary in Confluence, with the merged PR when implemented. Build only in the sprint the ticket is assigned to; each ticket keeps its own branch/PR and backend owners' work stays on their own tickets. [AL-192|https://alprojectcs3.atlassian.net/browse/AL-192] tracks unagreed contracts and uncovered V2 screens; this ticket does not silently absorb them.

As a *broker*, I want to see only the files of clients I referred, so that other brokers' clients stay private.

*Brief line:* Web: Role-Based Access: independent mortgage brokers restricted to viewing and managing only their referred client files.

# Opening another broker's client by URL shows "not found", because the Firestore rule refuses the read (not just the UI).
# A broker can open each of their clients' applications and see its status. Messaging the borrower: moved to the Sprint 2 broker inbox story (team decision, 19 Oct 2026).
# The list updates without refreshing when a borrower chooses this broker.

column1: As a borrower, I see how much I can borrow from my income, debts and deposit
column29:
h2. User story

As a *borrower*, I want to see how much I can borrow from my income, debts and deposit, so that I know my budget before I start looking at houses.

*Brief line:* Mobile: Affordability & Loan Application: forms capturing household annual gross income, existing debts, deposit and requested term.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Given valid inputs, the result shows the maximum loan, maximum property price, monthly repayment, the repayment if rates rise 2 points, and which limit applied ("limited by income (4x income)" or 3.5x for non-first-time buyers, "limited by deposit (90% LTV)" or "limited by debts (40% of income)").
# For the two reference cases on the affordability endpoint subtask (AL-57), at its 4.00% test rate, the app shows exactly the same figures as the endpoint.
# The rate used is shown with its month (for example "Average Irish new mortgage rate, Aug 2026: 3.9%") and labelled indicative, not an offer.
# Invalid inputs (negative amounts, a term outside 5 to 35 years) show an error under the field, and "Calculate" stays disabled until the form is valid.
# From the result, "Check a property" opens the property checker and "Start application" opens the application form with these inputs filled in.

h2. Decisions

* *Inputs:* single or joint, gross yearly income, monthly debts, deposit, term (5 to 35 years), first-time buyer. These are what the Central Bank lending limits depend on.
* *Joint applications (agreed with Nic on AL-57):* the app asks for each applicant's income, then adds them up and sends one household income to the endpoint. Debts are sent as one household total too.
* *Limits used:* a loan of up to 4x income for first-time buyers and 3.5x otherwise; *LTV of up to 90% for all buyers*; and the loan where the repayment at the rate plus 2 points, plus existing monthly debts, reaches 40% of gross monthly income. The maximum loan is whichever of the three is lowest. The first two are the Central Bank of Ireland's mortgage measures; the 40% cap is our prototype policy. _(Corrected in the backlog review: this said 80% for non-first-time buyers, but the Central Bank raised that to 90% on 1 Jan 2023.)_
* *Monthly debts (updated 12 Oct, confirmed by Nic on AL-57):* they do lower the maximum loan, through the 40% debt cap above. When that cap is the lowest limit, the result says "limited by debts (40% of income)". _(This used to say debts don't lower the maximum and are only judged by the credit committee. That contradicted AL-57.)_
* *Result:* maximum loan, maximum property price, monthly repayment, and the repayment if rates rise 2%. The borrower sees what they can afford and how sensitive it is to rates, which matches the underwriter's stress test.
* *Where it's calculated:* in the backend endpoint, not the app, so the app and the underwriter portal always agree.
* *Sign-in:* required. The endpoint checks the Firebase ID token, and results can be saved to the borrower's application.
* *Interest rate (decided in the backlog review):* the latest ECB benchmark rate for Irish new mortgages, the same rate the credit committee uses, shown with its month and labelled indicative. It replaces the fixed assumed rate that was still to agree.

h2. Test case

All figures use the affordability endpoint's 4.00% test rate.

# Single first-time buyer: €60,000 income, €0 debts, €40,000 deposit, 30 years. *Expect:* €240,000 "limited by income (4x income)", €280,000 price, €1,145.80 a month, "If rates rise 2%: €1,438.92 a month".
# Joint, not first-time buyers: €90,000 income (entered as two incomes that add up to it), €30,000 deposit, 25 years. *Expect:* €270,000 "limited by deposit (90% LTV)", €300,000, €1,425.16, €1,739.61.
# Single first-time buyer with debts: €60,000 income, €1,000 monthly debts, €50,000 deposit, 30 years. *Expect:* €166,792 "limited by debts (40% of income)", €216,792 price, €796.29 a month, "If rates rise 2%: €1,000.00 a month". (The stressed repayment plus €1,000 of debts is exactly 40% of €5,000 a month.)
# Enter €12,000,000 income, and step the term down from 5 and up from 35. *Expect:* "Enter an amount up to €10,000,000", the term stops at 5 and 35, and Calculate stays disabled.
# On the result. *Expect:* the rate shows with its month and is labelled indicative.
# Tap Start application. *Expect:* the application form is filled in from these inputs.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*Open point:* "Check a property" (criterion 5) opens the property checker, which is built in Sprint 2, so it can't be tested in Sprint 1. _(Resolved 12 Oct on AL-57: joint income is sent combined, and the 40% debt cap is confirmed, so case 3 and the Monthly debts decision were added.)_
{panel}

column1: As a borrower, I submit a loan application with my requested term and target property
column29:
h2. User story

As a *borrower*, I want to submit a mortgage application with my requested loan, term and target property, so that my broker and the bank can assess it.

*Brief line:* Mobile: Affordability & Loan Application (household gross income, existing debts, deposit, requested term).

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Given a completed affordability check, the application form is filled in from it and also asks for the loan amount, target property (from saved property checks), employment type, years in current job, monthly take-home pay and monthly living costs.
# A loan amount above the calculated maximum shows a warning, and a borrower with no saved property check is sent to the property checker first.
# Submitting asks for confirmation, then saves the application with status Applied and shows a reference number; a borrower with an active application can't start a second one.
# A draft can be edited freely; once submitted it's read-only, because the AI review starts straight away.
# The saved record matches the applications schema agreed with Dumi.

h2. Decisions

* *Product (changed 8 Oct):* mortgage in this story. HELOC is its own story (AL-195), pulled into Sprint 1 at planning on 7 Oct.
* *Target property:* chosen from the borrower's saved property checks, so every application has a model valuation. The underwriter's loan file compares the asking price against that valuation.
* *One active application per borrower.* It keeps the status screen and messaging simple.
* *Editing (changed in the backlog review):* editable while Draft, read-only once submitted (Applied), because the AI committee now starts automatically on submit. The earlier rule ("editable while Submitted, locked once broker review starts") relied on a Broker review status that isn't in the agreed status list. The edit-after-submit subtask is marked blocked until you decide what it becomes.
* *Take-home pay and living costs (added in the backlog review):* needed by the affordability agent to work out net disposable surplus, which the brief names.
* *Document uploads* (payslips, bank statements): not in scope for now; they would need Firebase Storage.

h2. Test case

# From a completed affordability check, enter €210,000, €3,650 take-home pay, €1,400 living costs, Employed, 4 years, and choose a saved property. *Expect:* the review shows these values. Confirm. *Expect:* status Applied and a reference number.

column1: As an underwriter, an affordability agent reports disposable surplus, stress-tested repayments and DTI
column29:
h2. User story

As an *underwriter*, I want an affordability agent to report the borrower's net disposable surplus, stress-tested repayment and DTI, so that I can see whether the loan is affordable today and if rates rise.

*Brief line:* Affordability Agent: evaluates net disposable surplus, stress-tested repayments and regulatory borrowing caps.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# For a synthetic application code (not the LLM) works out the monthly repayment at the benchmark mortgage rate, the repayment at +2 points, DTI and net disposable surplus at both rates, and loan-to-income against the Central Bank limit (4x first-time buyers, 3.5x others).
# Unit tests cover normal, zero-rate and stressed repayment, joint totals, missing or zero income and both sides of every band and cap boundary.
# Code sets the stressed DTI band (40% or less / up to 50% / over 50%) and the surplus band (EUR 500 or more / EUR 0 or more / below EUR 0) and passes them to the agent, and a test shows the agent's reply can't change a band or clear a cap breach.
# Given those figures the agent on Ollama returns JSON that passes our schema check: rating (strong / adequate / weak / unaffordable), recommendation (Approve / Conditionally Approve / Decline), concerns and conditions, quoting only figures it was given.
# A reply that fails the check is retried once with the error shown and if it fails again the run stops as failed, with no other provider used in its place.

h2. Notes

* Design: agent committee plan (al-ai docs), decisions A1, A7 to A10.
* The benchmark mortgage rate is the Irish new house-purchase rate (ECB series MIR.M.IE.B.A2C.A.R.A.2250.EUR.P).
* Needs monthly take-home pay and monthly living costs from the application form (asked for on the affordability and loan application stories).
* The calculations are shared with the affordability endpoint and the rate-shock simulator, so they live in one module (first subtask).

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Only the authorised minter can mint; a Hardhat test shows another account is refused.
# Minting the same application twice is rejected (test).
# Hardhat tests read back every stored field of a minted note.

15/Oct/26 10:15 AM;712020:0460d6e5-1deb-4aad-adf1-a3808b62ed5c;*Decisions for the loan note (from the blockchain breakdown, AL-168):*

# *ERC-721 via OpenZeppelin.* Each loan is a unique token, the base contract is standard and audited, and block explorers show it properly once it's on the testnet.
# *Stored on-chain per note:* principal in euro cents, APR in basis points (4.25% = 425), term in months, loan type (mortgage or HELOC), and a borrower reference.

# *Only the minter can mint:* OpenZeppelin {{AccessControl}} with a {{MINTER_ROLE}} held by al-core's wallet. Any other account is refused.

The ERC-721 choice and these reasons go in {{al-core/README.md}} with the contract (AL-170).

# FastAPI's {{/docs}} page lists every endpoint with its request and response.

h2. Original brief

The team picked FastAPI for the Python API. Once it can save to and read from the local database, web and mobile have a real interface to build against.

* A FastAPI app that checks the Firebase ID token on protected routes (Firebase Admin SDK, pointed at the emulators from AL-53)

* FastAPI's built-in {{/docs}} page, so web and mobile can see every request and response
* A short README with the run command and port

* *API or straight to Firestore:* Firebase lets the apps read and write Firestore directly under the security rules. Decide which actions go through the API and which don't.
* *How it runs:* Docker Compose alongside the emulators, or {{uv run fastapi dev}}.

h3. Done when

* Web and mobile owners can create and read an application through the API against the local emulators
* {{/docs}} lists every endpoint

Nic can pair on this or take part of it if needed.

# The local node runs through Docker Compose, as the brief suggests, or the README says why not.
# Private keys live only in {{.env}} (testnet wallets only), with empty names in {{.env.example}}.

h2. Scope change (18 Oct)

The criteria first said both contracts (loan note and audit registry). The audit registry belongs to the audit hash story (AL-36), which is in Sprint 2, and the Sprint 1 goal covers the loan note only, so it moved there. Agreed with Nic in #dev on 18 Oct. The deploy script and tests get the second contract with AL-36.

h2. Split (backlog review)

The "This week: break the blockchain stories down" part below is now its own Week 3 task, linked here, so this ticket is only the Hardhat setup (the ticket already said the setup can go into Sprint 1). The original text is kept below.

h2. Original brief

The blockchain half of al-core. The brief asks for a loan note contract (ERC-721 or a stateful contract holding principal, APR, term and a public borrower ID) and an audit registry that stores a SHA-256 hash of the credit memo, valuation and approval.

The breakdown and the choices below are for this week. The setup itself can go into sprint 1.

h3. This week: break the blockchain stories down (moved to its own task)

Same as everyone else: add subtasks to each story that pin down the details, and write what you chose, and why, on the story.

* *AL-34 Lifecycle:* which states live on-chain and which only in Firestore (Applied, AI Deliberated, Underwriter Approved, Funded, Closed)? Who may move a loan into each state? Can a state be skipped?
* *AL-35 Loan note:* ERC-721 or a plain stateful contract? Which fields go on-chain? What is the borrower's public identifier, and how does personal data stay off-chain?
* *AL-36 Audit hash:* which fields go into the hash, and in what format, so anyone can recompute it later? Can a stored hash ever be changed or deleted?

h3. Options to explore and document

Write what you chose, and why, in {{al-core/README.md}}.

* *Where the chain runs:* a local Hardhat node for development (port 8545 in {{docs/infrastructure.md}}). The live site on AWS can't reach a node on a laptop, the same problem as Ollama, so choose between a public testnet (Polygon Amoy or Arbitrum Sepolia, both allowed by the brief) and a Hardhat node running on AWS.
* *Who signs transactions:* the underwriter's own wallet in the browser (for example MetaMask with ethers.js), or the API signing with a key it holds (web3.py). This decides how Nikoloz builds sign-off (AL-37), so agree it with him.
* *Which library:* Ethers.js, Web3.py or both, depending on the answer above.

h3. Scope once the options are chosen

* A Hardhat project in {{al-core/}} with the two contracts and their tests (the audit registry now with AL-36)
* A deploy script that puts the contracts on the local node
* Run commands in {{al-core/README.md}}

Testnet wallets only. Private keys stay in {{.env}}, never in the repo.

h3. Done when

* {{npx hardhat node}} plus the deploy script puts the loan note contract on a local chain
* The contract tests pass

Nic can pair on this if needed.

column1: AI: test seed-bagged ensembles, GPBoost and TabPFN for the v2 valuation model
column29:
h2. What

The literature research found three model ideas worth one fair test each for the v2 valuation model (five inputs plus the Eircode routing key): averaging several seeds and models (bagging and the equal-average ensemble), GPBoost (boosting with county and routing-key random effects), and TabPFN (a pretrained model for small tables). Measure them against the single-model references on the development folds and say whether any is worth shipping.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Before any comparison runs, a config is committed with the variants, the references (HistGradientBoosting 22.23% and CatBoost 21.78% CV MAPE with the Eircode key), the settings, and the rule for what counts as worth adopting, including that estimates must not shift low.
# Each variant is scored on the same development rows and the same five group folds, with MAPE, MdAPE, within 10%, MAE, R2, and the median over or under estimate. Calibration and the final test are not read.
# TabPFN's model weights are downloaded only after the owner agrees, and the report records the licence and where the weights came from.
# The report says plainly whether any variant clears the rule, what it would cost to ship (models, dependencies, speed), and what the result means for the v2 plan.

h2. Notes

Nothing here changes the frozen v1 model or its final test. A v2 would be a new version with its own tuning and final test.

column29:
h2. Why

Found while reviewing PR 65 (the backend ticket for the queue fields). That PR adds {{ltvBand}} and {{riskTier}} to each application document, and AL-246 makes al-ai write them later. The portal queue today derives its band on the client from the valuation-based {{ltvPct}} and reads its tier from {{review/underwriting}}. The asking-price band and the valuation figure can put the same application in different bands (loan 300,000, asking price 400,000, valuation 360,000: 75% on the price, so {{80_or_less}}; 83% on the valuation, so {{80_to_90}}).

h2. Spec

Use the application document's stored {{ltvBand}} and {{riskTier}} for queue grouping. The band values are {{80_or_less}}, {{80_to_90}} and {{over_90}}, based on the asking price. Tiers are A to D.

For each field independently, keep the current behaviour only while that stored field is absent: the band falls back to the valuation-based {{ltvPct}}, the tier falls back to {{review/underwriting}}. Once a stored field exists it takes precedence. Label the displayed {{ltvPct}} as the valuation-based LTV and keep it separate from the stored asking-price band.

Scope: queue reads, grouping, labels and tests in {{al-web/}} only. Field production stays in the backend work.

Open questions to confirm with Dumi and Nic before implementation: how the agreed schema represents an unset field, and what the queue shows if a stored field exists with an invalid value (it must not silently fall back to the old source).

# With valid stored fields present, grouping uses {{ltvBand}} and {{riskTier}} from the application. A different tier in {{review/underwriting}} does not override the stored tier.
# Tests cover both fields absent and each field absent on its own. Only the absent field uses its current fallback. With neither source available, the existing missing-value group stays visible.
# A test application with stored {{ltvBand: over_90}} and valuation-based {{ltvPct: 85}} appears in the over-90 group, and its 85% is labelled as the valuation-based LTV.
# A live update that adds the stored fields moves the row and updates the group counts without a reload.

column1: Web: handle session faults and role changes while the portal is open
column29:
h2. Why

Found while reviewing the login pull request for AL-153. These behaviours are safe (they fail closed, and the security rules and API still use the fresh token) but they are the wrong experience, and two tests are missing. They are outside AL-153's scope, so they are raised here instead of growing that pull request.

h2. Spec

# *Session restore faults.* The Firebase {{onAuthStateChanged}} error callback is never called in the installed SDK, so the portal's {{error}} auth status and its page cannot happen. When the ID-token lookup fails (offline, expired token with no network, emulator stopped) the user lands on "Not allowed, ask an administrator". Show "We could not verify your session, reload to try again" with a retry for that case, and remove or document the unreachable {{error}} status.
# *Role change in an open tab.* The role is resolved only when the signed-in uid changes. Subscribe with {{onIdTokenChanged}} and re-resolve silently when the uid is unchanged (go to {{loading}} only on a uid change), so a role change reaches an open tab without a reload.
# *Small clean-ups from the same review.* Remove the unused {{state.from}} on the redirect to {{/login}}, or make it work with an allow-list; one {{portalHomeFor(role)}} helper instead of three copies; a {{loading}} branch on {{/forbidden}}; user-facing copy that does not say "Firebase".

h2. Acceptance criteria

# With the token lookup failing, a signed-in user sees the retry message, not the administrator message; a Vitest test covers it.
# A fake service that changes the role claim for the same uid moves the open page from {{/underwriter}} to "Not allowed" without a reload; a test covers it.
# A test defers one user's role resolution, delivers a different user (or a sign-out), then resolves the first, and asserts the page never shows the first user's role (the out-of-order race).
# A test drives the login form for an underwriter, for a borrower (refusal message) and for an already signed-in user opening {{/login}}.
# {{firebaseAuthService}} and {{firebase.ts}} have at least one test each (a stub user with {{getIdTokenResult}}; production config throws on a missing value and never connects the emulator).

18/Oct/26 10:43 PM;712020:eaa0b7b1-efef-47b1-b9ce-1f620c274091;Security review of the portal code on 18 Oct 2026 (a source review plus {{npm audit --omit=dev}}, which reported 0 vulnerabilities in 121 production dependencies). It found three things that belong in this ticket. None is exploitable across brokers today, because the Firestore rules remain the access boundary, and I have not reproduced any of them in a browser.

# *Role changes on a token refresh do not reach the route guard (medium).* {{authService.ts}} subscribes to {{onAuthStateChanged}}, which does not fire on a token refresh. If a user is downgraded and a refreshed token carries the new role, the guard can keep admitting the old routes until the next sign-in. Fix: subscribe to {{onIdTokenChanged}}, clear the old role and data while the new role resolves, and add a test with a same-user downgrade.
# *Sign-out does not clear the Firestore document cache (medium).* Sign-out unsubscribes the listeners and clears the React state, but the SDK's in-memory cache lives on in the page, and a new sign-in can show cached results before the server confirms them. With the current filters a broker can only see their own documents this way, so I did not find a cross-broker leak. Fix: tie the database instance to the session (terminate it on sign-out) and avoid showing cached results before the server confirms them. Test it with account switching and a broker reassignment.
# *A failed sign-out is invisible on the data pages (low).* The header swallows the rejection and the pages do not show the provider's error. Fix: show the safe message in the shared header as an accessible alert.

Also in scope here from the earlier note: 401 and 403 handling once the portal makes API calls. Not started, because this ticket is in the backlog and needs the team to pull it into a sprint.

18/Oct/26 10:55 PM;712020:eaa0b7b1-efef-47b1-b9ce-1f620c274091;Update 18 Oct, 22:55. The three fixes are done on a local branch ({{feature/AL-243-handle-session-faults}}, commit 519accf, based on current {{main}}). It is not pushed and there is no PR, because this ticket is still in the backlog and the team has been asked in #meetings whether to pull it into Sprint 1.

* *Token refresh:* the portal now listens for ID token changes. When the role changes for the same user, protected content is hidden while the new role resolves, an older check can never overwrite a newer one, and the page reloads once so access is evaluated from scratch.
* *Sign-out:* a successful sign-out reloads the page at {{/login}}, which drops the SDK's in-memory cache that React state cannot clear. Initial sign-in, a restored page and an unchanged role never trigger a reload.
* *Failed sign-out:* the safe message now shows beside the Sign out button on both pages (as an alert), and the session is kept.

Evidence: tests 30 to 42 (all pass, run twice), build passes, secret scan clean. Each fix has regression tests, and each fails when only that fix is removed. A second reviewer read the diff. Not tested: a real browser reload and the Firestore cache itself, because the Firestore client is not on {{main}} yet.

Known trade-offs: an unchanged role also hides content briefly while its refresh resolves (about once an hour), and a role removed entirely shows "Not allowed" without a reload; the reload happens at sign-out.

column1: Web: broker client list polish from the PR 68 review
column29:
h2. Why

The client list PR (#68) was approved by Ibrahima and Nic on 19 Oct 2026 with small non-blocking notes. They are recorded here so they do not get lost.

h2. Spec

# *Name fallback.* When a borrower changes broker, the old broker keeps the application but can no longer read the profile, so the row shows "Name unavailable". SCHEMA.md has {{borrowerName}} on each application for this case. Show {{application.borrowerName}} when there is no profile. Check first that {{borrowerName}} is on the seeded applications on {{main}}; if it is not, this waits for the core change.
# *Unreachable Firestore.* The page stays on "Loading your clients" forever when Firestore is unreachable. After a timeout, move to the existing error state.
# *Profiles read error.* Log the error code ({{console.warn}}) in the profiles error handler so a rules regression is visible.
# *Flaky test.* The test "shows no clients yet only once profiles have answered with nothing" timed out once on a cold run for Nic, and once for the independent reviewer before the PR was opened. Give its {{findBy}} calls a longer timeout, or remove the timing dependence.
# *Question for the team:* should brokers see Draft applications in the list? The borrower app now saves drafts, so half-filled ones will appear. Record the answer on this ticket.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# A client whose profile cannot be read shows its application's {{borrowerName}}; with neither, it still shows "Name unavailable". A test covers both.
# When Firestore does not answer within the timeout, the list shows the error state instead of loading forever. A test covers it with fake timers.
# A refused profiles query logs the error code once.
# The named test passes 20 times in a row on a cold run.
# The Drafts decision is written on this ticket and, if drafts are hidden, a test covers it.

Backlog until the team agrees to pull it into a sprint.

column1: Seed data: borrower names, the valuation model's property type spelling, and the real AI models
column29:
Three fixes to {{al-core/scripts/seed.js}}, done together so there is one re-seed and one export.

# *Borrower names.* {{borrowerName}} is in SCHEMA.md (copied onto the application when it is created) but the seeded applications don't have it. Nikoloz needs it to show the borrower's name in the underwriter queue (AL-32, agreed in #meetings on 19 Oct).
# *Property type spelling.* Raised by Nic on the submit-fields PR (#71): the seed uses {{propertyType: 'semi_detached'}}, but the valuation model only accepts {{Detached}}, {{Semi-D}}, {{Terrace}}, {{End of Terrace}}, {{Bungalow}}, {{Apartment}}, {{Duplex}} and {{Townhouse}} (from the data readiness report). The seed should use the model's spelling so a seeded application can be valued as-is. Validating {{property_type}} against this list on submit is a separate, later ticket.
# *AI call models.* Raised by Nic on the valuation model PR (#74): the seeded {{ai_calls}} still use the old plan (valuation on Gemini, Market & Macro on Groq Llama 3.3 70B, strategist on Mistral). The decision recorded in {{docs/infrastructure.md}} is Market & Macro and the strategist on Gemini, affordability on Ollama {{qwen3.5:9b}}, and valuation on Mistral Small 4 (Groq {{gpt-oss-120b}} only as a manual backup).

*Nic's answer (Slack, 19 Oct 19:40):* only the affordability agent exists, so {{qwen3.5:9b}} is the only real model string. The valuation, market and strategist agents aren't built yet, so seed them with the planned models by name for now and keep the names in one place so they're easy to change. Nic sends the exact model strings once those agents are working; swapping them in is a small follow-up.

Pulled into Sprint 1 because the seed is what the demo and the portal show; no story points (Task).

h2. Acceptance criteria

# Every seeded application has {{borrowerName}}, matching its borrower's {{fullName}}.
# Every seeded {{property.propertyType}} is one of the model's eight values ({{semi_detached}} becomes {{Semi-D}}).
# The seeded {{ai_calls}} use: affordability → {{ollama}} / {{qwen3.5:9b}}; valuation → {{mistral}} / Mistral Small 4; market → {{gemini}}; strategist → {{gemini}}. The three not-yet-built agents use the planned model names, defined in one place in seed.js with a comment saying they are placeholders until Nic confirms the exact strings.
# The audit records and their hashes are rebuilt from the new calls (seed.js does this), and the seed export is regenerated.
# {{node scripts/seed.js --dry-run}} still covers every status, LTV band and risk tier, and all al-core tests pass.
